pairs.locus: Asconius, In Cornelium (Pro Cornelio de maiestate, enarratio; Cicero quoted)
pairs.question: Legem de libertinorum suffragiis Cornelius C. Manilio dedit. Quid est hoc dedit? Attulit? an rogavit? an hortatus est?
pairs.answer: Attulisse ridiculum est, quasi legem aliquam aut ad scribendum difficilem aut ad excogitandum reconditam: quae lex paucis his annis non modo scripta sed etiam lata esset.
pairs.derivation: Asconius quotes Cicero verbatim. Cicero poses a rhetorical question about the word 'dedit' and answers it himself. The setup sentence 'Legem ... Cornelius C. Manilio dedit.' is kept verbatim so 'dedit' has a referent (rule 2); the speech tag 'inquit' (after 'Legem,') is dropped as framing/narration and the now-dangling comma normalized away. The question runs through the three sub-questions 'Attulit? an rogavit? an hortatus est?'. The answer is the contiguous reply that follows, ending at the first full stop after 'esset' (the interior colon is not a full stop, so the relative clause stays in).

pairs.question: Num in eo qui sint hi testes haesitatis?
pairs.answer: Duo reliqui sunt de consularibus, inimici tribuniciae potestatis.
pairs.derivation: Asconius quotes Cicero, who asks whether the audience is in doubt who these witnesses are and then identifies them himself. The non-answering preamble 'Ego vobis edam.' ('I will tell you') is skipped per the answer-window guidance; the answer's start is advanced to the operative sentence 'Duo reliqui sunt de consularibus, inimici tribuniciae potestatis.', ending at its full stop. The following 'Pauci praeterea adsentatores eorum atque adseculae subsequuntur.' is further elaboration and is cut.

pairs.locus: Asconius, In toga candida (enarratio; Cicero quoted)
pairs.question: Te vero, Catilina, consulatum sperare aut cogitare non prodigium atque portentum est? A quibus enim petis?
pairs.answer: A principibus civitatis? qui tibi, cum L. Volcacio cos. in consilio fuissent, ne petendi quidem potestatem esse voluerunt.
pairs.derivation: Asconius quotes Cicero, who asks from whom Catiline seeks the consulship and answers himself by enumeration. The inline page marker '(89)' at the line start is stripped as scaffolding. The question keeps the prior sentence as setup so 'petis' has a referent (the consulship). The answer is the contiguous remainder of the line answering 'from whom' (from the leaders, who refused him even the right to stand), Cicero's standard answer-by-proposing-and-refuting; it ends at the line's full stop. The subsequent enumerated answers (A senatoribus? / Ab equestri ordine? / A plebe?) are split across non-adjacent lines by Asconius's prose commentary and so are not stitched in (no interior ellipsis).
